conflict_resolutions.WHOLE_END_ACTOR_DISAGREEMENT: EO 14148 section 2 revokes this order whole on 2025-01-20; EO 14159 is a later instrument that does not give an earlier date and is recorded in the source notes. EO 14148 is the end actor.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 14010 is the official Federal Register text layer at 86 FR 8267, PDF pages 1-5 (Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 23 / Friday, February 5, 2021); it names Executive Order 14010 of February 2, 2021, Creating a Comprehensive Regional Framework To Address the Causes of Migration, To Manage Migration Throughout North and Central America, and To Provide Safe and Orderly Processing of Asylum Seekers a, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(u) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 14010 of February 2, 2021 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. Section 4(a)(ii)(F) revokes Presidential documents in the present tense: items (1) to (4) each form their own clause, and each is exhausted on issuance, 2021-02-02; item (5) lies in a clause that also holds the directive in paragraph (G), which runs until the order is revoked. savings.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 14010 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted. The revocations of the Presidential documents listed in section 4(a)(ii)(F), performed on 2021-02-02, are accrued effects that section 2 of Executive Order 14148 does not undo.
